title: "The dearest land"
hookLine: leaving, he says to Mecca: you are the dearest land to me, and if your people hadn't driven me out I'd never have left (Tirmidhi)

cards: The city that just tried to kill him is behind him now. Its leaders mocked him. Its council voted on his death.
Its young men waited at his door with swords. And as the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, leaves it, the hadith keep words he speaks to it. Not to the people.
To the place itself. Two companions report what he said, and both reports are kept in the collection of al-Tirmidhi. Today: Mecca.

teach.b: In one report, from Abdullah ibn Adi, the Prophet stands at a spot in Mecca and says: by God, you are the best of God's earth, and the dearest of God's earth to God.

teach.h: IF I HADN'T BEEN DRIVEN OUT.
teach.b: And if I had not been driven out of you, I would never have left. In the other, from Ibn Abbas, he speaks more personally: how good you are as a land, and how dear you are to me.
If my people had not driven me out, I would never have lived anywhere but you. Listen to the two halves. The first is pure love: dearest, best, how good you are.
The second names what happened, with no softening: I was driven out. He doesn't pretend he's leaving by choice. And he doesn't let what the people did turn into hatred for the place.
The Qur'an uses the same plain language: the town that drove you out.
Grief and love, and the truth about why, all in two sentences.

teach.h: THE TOWN THAT DROVE YOU OUT.
teach.b: Anyone who has left a hometown, a country, a house they grew up in, may know the shape of it.
You can love a place and still be forced to leave it, and you can say both out loud. Mecca will come back into his life later. Here, he says goodbye.

how: Many Muslims quote the Prophet's farewell to Mecca when they speak of love for one's homeland, and Mecca remains the city Muslims face in prayer and travel to on pilgrimage.

o: the town that welcomed him as its own
the city he called the dearest land
the place he chose to leave of his own will

games.q: you're leaving the city that tried to kill you. you stop at its edge. what do you say to it?
o: you are the dearest land to me.
games.why: he told Mecca it was the dearest land, and that he would never have left if his people hadn't driven him out.

practice: Let a place you've left come to you, a childhood home, a city, a room that isn't yours anymore, and walk through it slowly: the light, the smell, who was there.

If the reason you left still stings, let it be true without arguing with it, then silently tell the place what it was to you, in one or two plain sentences, the way he did. If you pray, you can thank God for that place.

wordCard.voice: Mecca. Leaving the city, the Prophet told it he would never have left if he hadn't been driven out, the dearest land to him. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: grief and love, both true. Neither one had to cancel the other. See you tomorrow.
